transcript:
Header:
Date: 2025-04-08
Start: 14:00 UTC
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Alyssa Chen (Redwood AE), Marco Ruiz (Redwood SE), Daniel Kwan (Redwood CSM), Priya Desai (Catalyst PM), Liam O'Connor (Catalyst ML Eng), Sana Malik (Catalyst Privacy), Raj Patel (Catalyst Data)

Summary:
Quick weekly POC sync reviewing quality eval results from last week's batch, discussing prompt-set regressions, guardrail tuning, and next steps to run a larger regression on Dedicated infra. Agreed to run 1k-sample regression and share scoring notebook and SOC2/security artifacts.

[00:00:00] Alyssa: hey everyone, thanks for joining on time. quick agenda — marco will run through the quality dashboard and the regression list, then we want to confirm the additional prompt sets priya said you'd upload, and close with next steps. sound good?

[00:00:23] Priya: yep that works, thanks. small note — sana wants to cover any new data residency or retention configs up front.

[00:00:35] Sana: hi, just a two minute check — the requirement is that any PHI-like examples in the pilot must be redacted and logs retained for 30 days, right? that was our ask.

[00:00:50] Alyssa: correct — redwood Dedicated gives you control over retention, and for Hosted we can set shorter retention but for the POC we'll use Dedicated so you can test actual behaviors. marco, you want to take it?

[00:01:05] Marco: yeah sure. pulling up the eval sheet here. uh I'm looking at the 250-sample run we did last thursday — it's the one with prompt variants v1-4. high-level: overall semantic-similarity score is at 0.78 using embedding cosine + human-weighted rubric. hallucination flag rate is about 9% across samples, but when we isolate the medical-context buckets it bumps to ~14%.

[00:01:40] Liam: can you remind me what counts as a hallucination in your scoring? sometimes our annotators mark minor factual drift as acceptable.

[00:01:50] Marco: good call — our automated tag is precision+entity mismatch: if generated text asserts a fact not supported by the context it triggers. then human adjudicators validated a subset. we also track false-positive guardrail triggers where the model refused but customer expected an answer.

[00:02:10] Priya: i noticed prompt variant 3 actually had lower hallucinations but worse fluency — it felt like the model clipped when uncertain. is that the tradeoff you saw?

[00:02:22] Marco: exactly. v3 uses stricter safety priming, which reduces hallucination but increases refusals/ellipsis. the metrics: v3 refusal rate 12% vs v1 4%, hallucination 5% vs 11%.

[00:02:40] Raj: are we scoring on ROUGE or something else? what metric mix should we weigh for the pilot decision?

[00:02:50] Marco: mix of metrics: semantic-similarity (embedding cosine), entity F1 for structured facts, a human-weighted acceptability score, and a penalty for hallucination. i'll share the scoring notebook so you can re-weight.

[00:03:05] Priya: can you also include a column for "user-impact severity"? our product team prioritizes high-severity hallucinations more than low-severity ones.

[00:03:15] Marco: will do.

[00:03:20] Sana: about retention — i need to confirm that audit logs and request/response pairs can be stored on your Dedicated infra under our VPC and that keys can be customer-managed.

[00:03:32] Alyssa: yes. Dedicated supports customer-managed KMS and VPC peering for the pilot; logs can be routed to your S3 endpoint. i'll follow up with the SOC2 doc that describes the controls.

[00:03:44] (small crosstalk)

[00:04:00] Marco: back to regressions — we identified 18 regression cases where v2->v4 substitutions produced worse entity extraction. many are prompt-sensitivity cases: slight rewording of the prompt yields model output that omits a crucial field. example: prompt asking for "patient allergy list" returned an empty list for 3 samples.

[00:04:25] Liam: do you think that's model variance or tokenization/kv cache issue? on smaller sequences we saw kv cash spikes — sorry, cache spikes — with quantized runs.

[00:04:38] Marco: good catch — there is known difference when using q4 quantization profile; we saw a small increase in tokenization misalignments on edge cases. our runtime's KV cache handling is the same but quantization can change softmax dynamics slightly. we'll run the same set on Dedicated without quantization to compare.

[00:04:58] Priya: what's the timeline for that? we need to show a reduction in regressions before next steering committee.

[00:05:05] Marco: we can kick off a 1k-sample batch run on Dedicated tomorrow if you give the green light, should finish in 24 hours. results and diff sheet by Friday morning.

[00:05:20] Priya: green light — please include both q4 and fp16 baselines.

[00:05:28] Marco: noted. i'll spin up both profiles.

[00:05:35] Daniel: quick note — we recommend enabling prefix/KV caching for the interactive flows because it reduces latency and costs; it won't change the model semantics much but can affect perf on long histories.

[00:05:48] Raj: any impact to quality from batching? our test harness batches short chats to save cost.

[00:05:55] Marco: batching shouldn't change outputs deterministically, but we observed rare token truncation if request sizes exceeded configured sequence windows. we'll validate batch-size config.

[00:06:10] Priya: about guardrails — we had a case where the model answered with a recommendation that technically could be construed as medical advice. we need deterministic refusals in those buckets. can Redwood's rule-based guardrail layer do that reliably?

[00:06:25] Marco: yes, we can put deterministic filters pre- or post-call. two patterns: safe-completion pre-prompt that instructs refusal, or post-filtering with the guardrail service that replaces or redacts outputs. for the POC we usually prototype both and pick the least disruptive approach.

[00:06:42] Priya: prefer post-filtering if possible — less brittle for hallucination cases.

[00:06:47] Marco: noted. i'll prototype a post-filter that checks entity hallucination and severity. we'll log false positives for tuning.

[00:06:55] Liam: curious about latency expectations on Dedicated for the 1k-run — median p95?

[00:07:03] Marco: on the Dedicated instance we're proposing, median is ~120-160ms per token for long context loads; p95 for typical workloads is under 600ms. for batched throughput tests we can push to higher TPS but with slightly higher tail latency. i'll include the perf config and exact instance types in the results.

[00:07:23] Sana: in terms of compliance, we need to know where telemetry goes and who has access. can you send an ACL mapping?

[00:07:31] Alyssa: yes — we'll send the security doc and a template ACL.

[00:07:40] (brief pause while Marco shares screen — link to eval spreadsheet posted: https://redwood.example.com/poc/catalyst/eval-2025-04-08.csv)

[00:08:10] Marco: walking through a couple of concrete examples — sample 47: prompt asked to summarize meds and the model invented a non-existent anticoagulant. flagged as high-severity hallucination. we re-ran v1 and v3; v3 refused which is safe but resulted in lower user-acceptance.

[00:08:35] Priya: that aligns with our user study — refusals are worse for support flows but fine for clinical decision support. we need route-based policies.

[00:08:45] Marco: yes, routing policy suggestion: for clinician flows prefer lower hallucination threshold and higher acceptance of refusal; for patient-facing flows prefer lower refusal and higher explainability. Redwood's routing can pick model variants per route.

[00:09:00] Raj: can we have per-route cost estimates? this will affect whether we run everything on Dedicated.

[00:09:07] Alyssa: we'll include a token-level cost projection with batching assumptions in the pricing sheet.

[00:09:15] Priya: one more thing — we have a prompt-set called "clarify-first" that asks the model to ask a clarifying question before answering ambiguous prompts. the v4 model seems to ignore that prompt in certain syntactic variants.

[00:09:30] Marco: that's likely prompt-sensitivity. i'll add the clarify-first variants to the regression set and include those permutations in the 1k run.

[00:09:40] Liam: when you run the 1k, include distributional sampling so we get both typical and edge-case prompts.

[00:09:47] Marco: yes we'll stratify by bucket (clinical, admin, patient).

[00:09:55] (noise/overlap)

[00:10:05] Priya: ok, security QA — sana, anything further?

[00:10:08] Sana: just confirm that SSO can be enforced for consoles and that logs are encrypted at rest using our KMS. also need to see pen-test reports.

[00:10:18] Alyssa: we'll provide SSO SAML config, KMS integration guide, and pen-test summary.

[00:10:25] Marco: operationally, if we detect a regression spike we'll auto-roll back to previous model variant on that route; that's part of the rollout policy. we've tested it in a canary flow.

[00:10:36] Priya: good — please document the rollback criteria and the alerting thresholds.

[00:10:40] Marco: will add to the runbook.

[00:10:45] Raj: about the scoring notebook — can we get it as a runnable colab or binder so our data team can re-run locally?

[00:10:52] Marco: yes — i'll push a notebook and script to the repo; link in slack.

[00:10:58] Alyssa: let's recap next steps so everyone is clear.

[00:11:02] Marco: 1) run 1k-sample regression on Dedicated with q4 and fp16 configs; include clarify-first variants and stratified buckets. 2) produce diff sheet highlighting the 18 current regressions plus any new ones. deliver by 2025-04-11.

[00:11:18] Priya: 3) we (Catalyst) will upload updated prompt sets and annotate top 50 failure cases by 2025-04-10.

[00:11:25] Alyssa: 4) i'll send SOC2, pen-test summary, SSO/KMS guides and the pilot pricing sheet by 2025-04-09.

[00:11:32] Daniel: 5) Redwood: prototype post-filter guardrail and log false-positives for tuning, include runbook for rollback.

[00:11:40] Priya: perfect. anything else?

[00:11:43] Raj: one small ask — can you also include a sample of labeled human adjudications so we can calibrate our annotators?

[00:11:50] Marco: yup, i'll include a gold set of 100 adjudicated samples.

[00:11:55] (wrap up)

[00:12:00] Alyssa: thanks everyone. i'll follow up with calendar for next week's sync same time. Marco will post links and the notebook in slack. Priya/Sana you'll get the security docs.

[00:12:12] Priya: thanks.

[00:12:15] (call ends, off-record chatter)

Notes: Transcript contains typical minor transcription errors (e.g., "KV cash" instead of "KV cache", "Redwood Dedicate" as heard). Links shared: eval CSV (see above) and notebook placeholder: https://redwood.example.com/poc/catalyst/eval-notebook

Recap / explicitly listed next steps (for calendar invite):
- Marco: run regression benchmarking (q4 vs fp16) on Dedicated; share diff and perf metrics by 2025-04-11
- Priya: upload prompt sets + annotate top failure cases by 2025-04-10
- Alyssa: share SOC2/pen-test/SSO-KMS docs and pilot pricing by 2025-04-09
- Marco: push scoring notebook and gold adjudication set to repo by 2025-04-09

End of transcript.
